example.pinyin: Tā xīnzhōng huìnù, què bùgǎn yán.
example.english: He was enraged inside, but dared not speak.
example.fact: 恚 is a classical-Chinese word for rage, now essentially obsolete in modern speech, surviving mainly in the Buddhist term 嗔恚 (chēnhuì), one of the "three poisons" said to cause suffering.

components.note: 白 (white) — 皑 describes something brilliantly white, like snow.
岂 (qǐ) gives a sound now quite distant from 皑's reading ái — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 山顶上白雪皑皑。
example.pinyin: Shāndǐng shàng báixuě áiái.
example.english: The mountaintop is covered in gleaming white snow.
example.fact: 皑 appears almost only in the poetic phrase 白雪皑皑 (báixuě áiái), describing an expanse of dazzling white snow, common in classical and descriptive writing about winter landscapes.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 锵 imitates the clanging sound of metal.
将 (jiāng) gives a sound close to 锵's reading qiāng, sharing the final and tone but with the initial consonant shifted.

example.hanzi: 他的演讲铿锵有力。
example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjiǎng kēngqiāng yǒulì.
example.english: His speech was powerful and resonant.
example.fact: 锵 is an onomatopoeic character imitating the clang of metal or bells, and appears in 铿锵有力 (kēngqiāng yǒulì), a phrase praising speech or writing as forceful and resonant, like the ringing of metal.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 簌 is associated with the rustling sound of bamboo or leaves.
欶 gives a sound related to 簌's reading sù, sharing the tone but with the initial consonant and vowel shifted.

example.hanzi: 眼泪簌簌地落下来。
example.pinyin: Yǎnlèi sùsù de luò xiàlái.
example.english: Tears fell down in a steady trickle.
example.fact: 簌簌 (sùsù) is an onomatopoeic word imitating a soft, continuous rustling or dripping sound, used poetically for falling leaves, snow, or tears.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 焙 describes drying or cooking something over low heat.
咅 (pǒu) gives a sound now quite distant from 焙's reading bèi — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 咖啡豆需要经过烘焙才能使用。
example.pinyin: Kāfēidòu xūyào jīngguò hōngbèi cáinéng shǐyòng.
example.english: Coffee beans need to be roasted before they can be used.
example.fact: 焙 appears mainly in 烘焙 (hōngbèi, "to bake/roast"), a word that covers both roasting coffee beans and baking bread or pastries — one general verb for two very different Western culinary techniques.

etymologyHint: The sun 日 high in the sky 天

components.note: 日 (sun) — represents the sun.
天 (sky) — combined with 'sun,' depicts the sun high in a vast sky, giving 昊 its meaning "vast, boundless heaven."

example.hanzi: 他的名字叫"王昊"。
example.pinyin: Tā de míngzi jiào "Wáng Hào".
example.english: His name is "Wang Hao."
example.fact: 昊 means "the vast sky" and, like 宇 and 天, is a popular character in Chinese given names for boys, chosen to evoke grandeur and boundlessness.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鹳 names a large wading bird, the stork.
雚 (guàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 鹳's reading.

example.hanzi: 鹳是一种大型涉水鸟类。
example.pinyin: Guàn shì yī zhǒng dàxíng shèshuǐ niǎolèi.
example.english: The stork is a large wading bird.
example.fact: 鹳 (storks) build enormous stick nests that they reuse and add to year after year, sometimes growing to weigh hundreds of kilograms after decades of continuous use.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 睽 describes staring, an eye-related action.
癸 (guǐ) gives a sound related to 睽's reading kuí, sharing the final's shape but with the initial consonant and tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他在众目睽睽之下摔倒了。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhòngmù kuíkuí zhīxià shuāidǎole.
example.english: He fell down right in front of everyone's watching eyes.
example.fact: 睽 appears mainly in 众目睽睽 (zhòngmù kuíkuí), a vivid idiom for being watched by many staring eyes at once, often used when someone is embarrassed in public.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刽 describes cutting or amputating with a blade.
会 (huì) gives a sound close to 刽's reading guì, sharing the final and tone but with the initial consonant shifted.

example.hanzi: 古代的刽子手负责执行死刑。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài de guìzishǒu fùzé zhíxíng sǐxíng.
example.english: Ancient executioners were responsible for carrying out death sentences.
example.fact: 刽 appears almost only in 刽子手 (guìzishǒu, "executioner"), a word also used figuratively today for anyone seen as responsible for destroying something valuable.

components.note: 鱼 (fish/aquatic creature) — 鳖 names an aquatic animal, the softshell turtle.
敝 (bì) gives a sound related to 鳖's reading biē, sharing the initial consonant but with the vowel and tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 鳖是一种可以食用的水生动物。
example.pinyin: Biē shì yī zhǒng kěyǐ shíyòng de shuǐshēng dòngwù.
example.english: The softshell turtle is an edible aquatic animal.
example.fact: 鳖 (softshell turtle) is prized in Chinese cuisine and traditional medicine as a nutritious delicacy, often stewed into a soup believed to be especially nourishing for recovery after illness.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 噎 describes choking, something blocking the throat.
壹 (yī) gives a sound related to 噎's reading yē, sharing the initial and tone but with the vowel shifted.

example.hanzi: 他吃得太快,被噎住了。
example.pinyin: Tā chī de tài kuài, bèi yē zhùle.
example.english: He ate too fast and choked.
example.fact: 噎 describes choking on food, and appears in the idiom 因噎废食 (yīn yē fèi shí, "to give up eating for fear of choking"), a warning against overreacting to one setback by abandoning something entirely.

meanings: modal particle indicating lack of enthusiasm

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 呗 is a sentence-final spoken particle.
贝 (bèi) gives a sound very close to 呗's reading bei, differing mainly in that 呗 is pronounced with a neutral tone.

example.hanzi: 不想去就别去呗。
example.pinyin: Bùxiǎng qù jiù bié qù bei.
example.english: If you don't want to go, then just don't, no big deal.
example.fact: 呗 is a colloquial sentence-final particle that softens a suggestion into something casual and obvious, roughly like adding "then, I guess" to the end of an English sentence.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 寰 relates to a domain or realm, an enclosed territory.
睘 (huán) gives the sound — an exact match with 寰's reading.

example.hanzi: 这项发明震惊了寰宇。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng fāmíng zhènjīngle huányǔ.
example.english: This invention astonished the whole world.
example.fact: 寰 is a literary word for "the whole world," appearing in 寰宇 (huányǔ) and sharing its root idea with 环球 (huánqiú, "global") — both built around the concept of an all-encompassing circle or domain.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 唷 is a spoken interjection.
育 (yù) gives a sound now quite distant from 唷's reading yō — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 唷,你怎么来了!
example.pinyin: Yō, nǐ zěnme láile!
example.english: Oh! You came!
example.fact: 唷 is a pure interjection expressing mild surprise, part of the same "mouth radical" family as 哦, 嗳, and 呀 — characters built solely to capture spoken exclamations.

components.note: 歹 (death/bad) — 殡 relates to death and funeral rites.
宾 (bīn) gives a sound close to 殡's reading bìn, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 殡仪馆负责办理丧葬事宜。
example.pinyin: Bìnyíguǎn fùzé bànlǐ sāngzàng shìyí.
example.english: The funeral home is responsible for handling funeral arrangements.
example.fact: 殡 appears mainly in 殡仪馆 (bìnyíguǎn, "funeral home") and 出殡 (chūbìn, "to hold a funeral procession"), both centered on the formal handling of a death.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淖 describes wet mud or slush.
卓 (zhuó) gives a sound now quite distant from 淖's reading nào — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 他陷入了债务的泥淖。
example.pinyin: Tā xiànrùle zhàiwù de nínào.
example.english: He fell into a quagmire of debt.
example.fact: 淖 appears mainly in 泥淖 (nínào), literally "mire, quagmire," and figuratively used for being stuck in a difficult, hard-to-escape situation, like debt or a moral dilemma.

etymologyHint: To verbally 讠 inform 告; 告 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech) — represents speech; 诰 describes a formal, spoken proclamation.
告 (to announce) — combined with 'speech,' emphasizes formally proclaiming something. 告 (gào) is also an exact phonetic match for 诰's reading.

example.hanzi: 皇帝下诰任命新的官员。
example.pinyin: Huángdì xià gào rènmìng xīn de guānyuán.
example.english: The emperor issued a proclamation appointing new officials.
example.fact: 诰 names a formal proclamation historically issued by an emperor, seen in 诰命 (gàomìng), an official document that could also bestow honorary titles on the mothers and wives of high officials.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恣 describes unrestrained self-indulgence, a matter of will.
次 (cì) gives a sound related to 恣's reading zì, sharing the final and tone but with the initial consonant shifted.

example.hanzi: 他恣意妄为,不顾后果。
example.pinyin: Tā zìyì wàngwéi, bùgù hòuguǒ.
example.english: He acts recklessly and willfully, without regard for consequences.
example.fact: 恣 appears mainly in 恣意 (zìyì, "as one pleases, wantonly"), always carrying a negative undertone of unchecked self-indulgence without regard for rules or others.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 睐 describes a glance, an eye-related action.
来 (lái) gives a sound close to 睐's reading lài, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这个产品受到了消费者的青睐。
example.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn shòudàole xiāofèizhě de qīnglài.
example.english: This product has received favor from consumers.
example.fact: 睐 appears mainly in 青睐 (qīnglài, "favor, approval"), literally referring to a favorable glance, now the standard word in Chinese marketing and news for describing something being well-received.

meanings: used in 嬋娟|婵娟[chan2 juan1] and 嬋媛|婵媛[chan2 yuan2]

components.note: 女 (woman) — 婵 describes feminine grace and beauty.
单 (dān) gives a sound related to 婵's reading chán, sharing the final but with the initial consonant and tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 苏东坡写道:"但愿人长久,千里共婵娟。"
example.pinyin: Sū Dōngpō xiě dào: "Dàn yuàn rén chángjiǔ, qiānlǐ gòng chánjuān."
example.english: Su Dongpo wrote: "May we live long, and share this beautiful moonlight though a thousand miles apart."
example.fact: 婵 appears mainly in 婵娟 (chánjuān), a poetic word for gracefulness that also serves as a classical name for the moon, most famously in Su Dongpo's line from his poem "水调歌头."

components.note: 木 (tree) — 榈 names a type of tree, the palm.
闾 (lǘ) gives the sound — an exact match with 榈's reading.

example.hanzi: 棕榈树生长在热带地区。
example.pinyin: Zōnglǘ shù shēngzhǎng zài rèdài dìqū.
example.english: Palm trees grow in tropical regions.
example.fact: 榈 appears only in 棕榈 (zōnglǘ, "palm tree"); palms are found naturally on every continent except Antarctica, from tropical rainforests to a few hardy species native to Mediterranean Europe.

components.note: 气 (gas) — helium is a gaseous element.
亥 (hài) gives the sound — an exact match with 氦's reading.

example.hanzi: 氦气球比空气轻,会往上飘。
example.pinyin: Hàiqìqiú bǐ kōngqì qīng, huì wǎng shàng piāo.
example.english: Helium balloons are lighter than air and will float upward.
example.fact: Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe after hydrogen, yet it's rare on Earth because it's light enough to escape into space over time.

components.note: 革 (leather) — 靳's original meaning was a leather strap on a horse's harness.
斤 (jīn) gives a sound close to 靳's reading jìn, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他姓靳,是我的同事。
example.pinyin: Tā xìng Jìn, shì wǒ de tóngshì.
example.english: His surname is Jin; he's my colleague.
example.fact: 靳 survives today almost entirely as a Chinese surname, its original meaning — a strap on a horse's harness — having fallen out of everyday use.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蛹 names a stage of insect development, the pupa.
甬 (yǒng) gives the sound — an exact match with 蛹's reading.

example.hanzi: 毛毛虫会变成蛹,再变成蝴蝶。
example.pinyin: Máomaochóng huì biànchéng yǒng, zài biànchéng húdié.
example.english: Caterpillars turn into pupae, then turn into butterflies.
example.fact: Inside a pupa (蛹), an insect undergoes complete metamorphosis, essentially dissolving most of its own tissues and rebuilding its body almost entirely from scratch before emerging as an adult.

meanings: used in 鴛鴦|鸳鸯[yuan1 yang1]

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鸯 names the female mandarin duck.
央 (yāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 鸯's reading.

example.hanzi: 公园的湖里有一对鸳鸯。
example.pinyin: Gōngyuán de hú lǐ yǒu yī duì yuānyāng.
example.english: There is a pair of mandarin ducks in the park's lake.
example.fact: 鸯 never appears alone — like several duck and bird-name characters, it exists only as half of the compound 鸳鸯, always naming the female specifically, while 鸳 names the male.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 惬 describes an emotional state, satisfaction.
夹 (jiā) gives a sound now quite distant from 惬's reading qiè — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 躺在沙滩上晒太阳,感觉很惬意。
example.pinyin: Tǎng zài shātān shàng shài tàiyáng, gǎnjué hěn qièyì.
example.english: Lying on the beach sunbathing feels very pleasant and satisfying.
example.fact: 惬 appears mainly in 惬意 (qièyì), a word for a comfortable, satisfying feeling of contentment, commonly used to describe relaxing experiences like a good meal or a lazy afternoon.

components.note: 戚 (grief, sorrow) — 蹙 relates to a distressed, worried expression.
足 (zú) gives a sound related to 蹙's reading cù, sharing the vowel and consonant class but differing in aspiration and tone.

example.hanzi: 她蹙眉思考着这个难题。
example.pinyin: Tā cùméi sīkǎozhe zhège nántí.
example.english: She furrowed her brow, thinking about this difficult problem.
example.fact: 蹙 describes knitting the brows in worry or concentration, as in 蹙眉 (cùméi), a more literary alternative to the everyday phrase 皱眉头 (zhòu méitóu).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诙 describes joking, a mode of speech.
灰 (huī) gives the sound — an exact match with 诙's reading.

example.hanzi: 他说话很诙谐,大家都喜欢和他聊天。
example.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn huīxié, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan hé tā liáotiān.
example.english: He speaks in a witty, humorous way, and everyone likes chatting with him.
example.fact: 诙 appears mainly in 诙谐 (huīxié), describing a witty, good-humored way of speaking that makes others enjoy someone's company.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眈 describes staring intently, an eye-related action.
冘 is a rare component whose own reading is unclear, making it hard to judge with confidence how close its sound is to 眈's reading dān.

example.hanzi: 竞争对手对这个市场虎视眈眈。
example.pinyin: Jìngzhēng duìshǒu duì zhège shìchǎng hǔshì dāndān.
example.english: Competitors are eyeing this market covetously, like tigers watching their prey.
example.fact: 眈 survives almost only in 虎视眈眈 (hǔshì dāndān), a vivid four-character idiom comparing a covetous stare to a tiger stalking its prey before pouncing.

meanings: the name of a certain stars
the god who is supposed to live in them

components.note: 罒 (net) — 罡 relates to a celestial pattern, imagined like a net of stars.
正 (zhèng) gives a sound now quite distant from 罡's reading gāng — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 《水浒传》中的一百零八位好汉对应三十六天罡和七十二地煞。
example.pinyin: "Shuǐhǔ Zhuàn" zhōng de yìbǎi líng bā wèi hǎohàn duìyìng sānshíliù Tiāngāng hé qīshí'èr Dìshà.
example.english: The 108 heroes in "Water Margin" correspond to the Thirty-Six Heavenly Generals and Seventy-Two Earthly Fiends.
example.fact: 罡 names a group of stars in Taoist astrology, most famously the "36 Heavenly Generals" (三十六天罡) that the classic novel Water Margin (水浒传) associates with 36 of its 108 outlaw heroes.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缮's original meaning involved mending cloth, extended to repairing in general.
善 (shàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 缮's reading.

example.hanzi: 这座古庙正在修缮。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔmiào zhèngzài xiūshàn.
example.english: This ancient temple is currently being repaired.
example.fact: 缮 appears mainly in 修缮 (xiūshàn), the formal word for repairing or renovating a building, especially one of historical or cultural value.

etymologyHint: A small 幺 child ⺼ leaving the womb 儿

components.note: 幺 (small, tiny) — represents something small, like a young child.
儿 (child) — combined with the body radical, depicts a child being born, giving 胤 its meaning "heir, descendant."

example.hanzi: 雍正皇帝原名爱新觉罗·胤禛。
example.pinyin: Yōngzhèng Huángdì yuánmíng Àixīnjuéluó·Yìnzhēn.
example.english: The Yongzheng Emperor's original name was Aisin Gioro Yinzhen.
example.fact: 胤 means "heir, descendant," and appears in the birth names of several Qing-dynasty princes, including 胤禛 (Yinzhen), who later became the Yongzheng Emperor — all of Emperor Kangxi's many sons shared the character 胤 in their given names.

meanings: the high land along a river

components.note: 夲 (tāo) gives a sound related to 皋's reading gāo, sharing the final and tone but with the initial consonant shifted.

example.hanzi: 皋陶是传说中的司法之神。
example.pinyin: Gāoyáo shì chuánshuō zhōng de sīfǎ zhī shén.
example.english: Gao Yao is the legendary god of justice.
example.fact: 皋 is best known from 皋陶 (Gao Yao), a legendary minister of justice under the sage-king Shun, still honored today as a mythical founding figure of Chinese law and jurisprudence.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蛀 describes damage caused by insects.
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 蛀's reading zhù, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服被虫蛀了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu bèi chóng zhùle.
example.english: This piece of clothing was eaten through by insects.
example.fact: 蛀 describes insect damage to materials like wood, books, or clothing, as in 蛀虫 (zhùchóng, "wood-boring insect"), a word also used metaphorically for a corrupt person secretly damaging an organization from within.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偌 is a demonstrative word originally describing a person's manner, 'thus, so.'
若 (ruò) gives the sound — an exact match with 偌's reading.

example.hanzi: 偌大的房子只住着一个人。
example.pinyin: Ruòdà de fángzi zhǐ zhùzhe yī gè rén.
example.english: Such a big house, yet only one person lives in it.
example.fact: 偌 appears almost only in 偌大 (ruòdà), a word emphasizing surprising largeness, often used with a hint of contrast, like a huge house with hardly anyone in it.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 疵 describes a flaw or blemish, likened to a minor ailment.
此 (cǐ) gives a sound close to 疵's reading cī, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这件产品有一些小瑕疵。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chǎnpǐn yǒu yīxiē xiǎo xiácī.
example.english: This product has some small flaws.
example.fact: 疵 pairs with 瑕 (also meaning "flaw," originally about jade) to form 瑕疵 (xiácī), the standard modern word for a minor defect or blemish in a product or plan.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — 绛 originally described the color of dyed silk.
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 绛's reading.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条绛色的裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yī tiáo jiàngsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She's wearing a deep-red skirt.
example.fact: 绛 names a deep, purplish red, one of many highly specific traditional Chinese color terms (alongside 朱, 赭, 绯) that distinguish shades English typically just lumps together as "red."

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 葆's original meaning involved dense foliage.
保 (bǎo) gives the sound — an exact match with 葆's reading.

example.hanzi: 他希望能永葆青春。
example.pinyin: Tā xīwàng néng yǒngbǎo qīngchūn.
example.english: He hopes to stay forever young.
example.fact: 葆 means "to preserve, keep," most often seen in the wish 永葆青春 (yǒngbǎo qīngchūn, "to forever preserve youth"), a common phrase in birthday wishes and advertising for beauty products.

meanings: short name for Guizhou 貴州|贵州[Gui4 zhou1]

components.note: 黑 (black) — 黔's literal meaning is 'black.'
今 (jīn) gives a sound now quite distant from 黔's reading qián — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: "黔" 是贵州省的简称。
example.pinyin: "Qián" shì Guìzhōu Shěng de jiǎnchēng.
example.english: "Qian" is the abbreviation for Guizhou Province.
example.fact: 黔 is the one-character abbreviation for Guizhou province, seen on Chinese license plates; its literal meaning is "black," though the exact historical reason behind pairing this meaning with the region is debated.

etymologyHint: A hedgehog's 彖 mouth 口

components.note: 口 (mouth) — represents a mouth.
彖 (a boar-like creature in ancient depictions) — combined with 'mouth,' depicts an animal's snout or beak, giving 喙 its meaning.

example.hanzi: 证据确凿,他无可置喙。
example.pinyin: Zhèngjù quèzáo, tā wúkě zhìhuì.
example.english: The evidence was conclusive, and he had nothing to say against it.
example.fact: 喙 means "beak" or "snout," and survives in modern Chinese mainly in the idiom 无可置喙 (wúkě zhìhuì, literally "no room to insert one's beak"), meaning someone has no grounds left to argue or object.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烽 names a signal fire.
夆 (féng) gives a sound close to 烽's reading fēng, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 古代边境用烽火传递军情。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài biānjìng yòng fēnghuǒ chuándì jūnqíng.
example.english: In ancient times, border regions used beacon fires to relay military information.
example.fact: 烽 names the beacon fires historically lit along the Great Wall to relay warnings of invasion across vast distances within minutes, and 烽火 today also means "the flames of war" metaphorically.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 儡 names a figure resembling a person, a puppet.
畾 (léi) gives a sound close to 儡's reading lěi, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 傀儡戏是中国一种古老的木偶表演艺术。
example.pinyin: Kuǐlěixì shì Zhōngguó yī zhǒng gǔlǎo de mù'ǒu biǎoyǎn yìshù.
example.english: Puppet theater is an ancient Chinese art of marionette performance.
example.fact: 儡 exists only as the second half of 傀儡 (kuǐlěi, "puppet"), and traditional Chinese puppet theater (傀儡戏) is one of the oldest forms of puppetry in the world, with records dating back over two thousand years.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 佼 describes a person's good looks or excellence.
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 佼's reading jiǎo, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他是同龄人中的佼佼者。
example.pinyin: Tā shì tónglíngrén zhōng de jiǎojiǎozhě.
example.english: He is a standout among his peers.
example.fact: 佼 appears mainly in 佼佼者 (jiǎojiǎozhě), a term for someone who clearly stands out from their peers in ability or achievement, similar to the English "cream of the crop."

meanings: used in 斑斕|斑斓[ban1 lan2]

components.note: 文 (pattern, decoration) — 斓 describes a rich, decorative array of colors.
阑 (lán) gives the sound — an exact match with 斓's reading.

example.hanzi: 秋天的树叶色彩斑斓。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de shùyè sècǎi bānlán.
example.english: Autumn leaves are riotously colorful.
example.fact: 斓 appears almost only in 斑斓 (bānlán), a vivid word for something dazzlingly multicolored, often describing autumn leaves, butterfly wings, or tiger stripes.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 嫔 names a rank of imperial concubine, a court woman.
宾 (bīn) gives a sound related to 嫔's reading pín, sharing the final but with the initial consonant and tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 嫔妃是古代皇帝的妃子。
example.pinyin: Pínfēi shì gǔdài huángdì de fēizi.
example.english: Consorts were the emperor's concubines in ancient times.
example.fact: 嫔 names a specific rank within the elaborate hierarchy of imperial concubines (嫔妃) in dynastic China, a system with many formally ranked tiers below the empress, similar in structure to a court bureaucracy.

components.note: 页 (head) — 颚 names a part of the head, the jaw.
咢 (è) gives the sound — an exact match with 颚's reading.

example.hanzi: 鲨鱼的颚非常有力。
example.pinyin: Shāyú de è fēicháng yǒulì.
example.english: A shark's jaw is extremely powerful.
example.fact: 颚 names the jaw, and shark jaws are especially famous for exerting some of the strongest bite forces of any living animal, made possible by cartilage that flexes rather than shatters under pressure.

components.note: 齿 (teeth) — 龈 relates to the mouth and teeth area, whether meaning 'gums' or the action of gnawing near the teeth.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound related to 龈's reading kěn, sharing the final's nasal ending but with the initial consonant and tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 狗喜欢龈骨头。
example.pinyin: Gǒu xǐhuan kěn gǔtou.
example.english: Dogs like to gnaw on bones.
example.fact: 龈 has two lives: as kěn it's an old variant of 啃 ("to gnaw"), while its far more common modern reading yín names the gums, as in 牙龈 (yáyín, "gums") — one character quietly carrying two unrelated meanings and sounds.

components.note: 皿 (dish/vessel) — 盅 names a small drinking vessel.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 盅's reading.

example.hanzi: 他倒了一盅茶。
example.pinyin: Tā dàole yī zhōng chá.
example.english: He poured a small cup of tea.
example.fact: 盅 names a small, handleless cup, most often seen today as the vessel for 茶盅 (chá zhōng, "tea cup") in traditional Chinese tea sets.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 娓's original sense described agreeable, pleasant speech or manner.
尾 (wěi) gives the sound — an exact match with 娓's reading.

example.hanzi: 老师娓娓道来这个历史故事。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī wěiwěi dàolái zhège lìshǐ gùshì.
example.english: The teacher told this historical story in an engaging, unhurried way.
example.fact: 娓 appears mainly in 娓娓道来 (wěiwěi dàolái), a phrase for storytelling that flows smoothly and pleasantly, often used to praise a speaker's engaging, unhurried style.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坂 names a hillside, a landform.
反 (fǎn) gives a sound related to 坂's reading bǎn, sharing the final and tone but with the initial consonant shifted.

example.hanzi: 坂本是一个常见的日本姓氏。
example.pinyin: Bǎnběn shì yī gè chángjiàn de Rìběn xìngshì.
example.english: Sakamoto is a common Japanese surname.
example.fact: 坂 means "hillside slope" and today is most recognizable in Japanese personal names like 坂本 (Sakamoto) and 松坂 (Matsuzaka), since Japan retained this character commonly in surnames referencing terrain.
